findings.description: A case that dies without printing a cost is now charged its cap against `remaining`, but the closing tally still sums `cost_usd ?? 0`. One crashed case can make the run print "N skipped for budget" next to a "spent $X" well below `--budget`. Sum the same `?? cap` charge in the tally, or label the figure as reported spend only.

The README says "a case that dies before reporting its cost is charged its full $5 cap", but the code charges `cap = Math.min(CASE_BUDGET_USD, remaining)`, which is less than $5 once under $5 remains. A case that throws before `review()` is charged nothing. Suggested wording: "a case whose run reports no cost is charged its cap (up to $5)".

LOCAL_DENY only removes `gh pr checkout*` from the skill's `allowed-tools`. The skill's unscoped `Read` (plus `Glob`/`Grep`) still works locally, where CI's `allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly` would void it, so the local reviewer can read e.g. `~/.config/gh/hosts.yml`. Also, the scrub comment "never sees the operator's tokens" overstates it, since the workflow notes `GH_TOKEN` survives the scrub. Consider adding a home-directory `Read` deny and narrowing the comment.

The LOCAL_DENY comment's "It would swap the config back." has no clear referent and doesn't say which config replaces which. Spell it out, e.g. "`gh pr checkout` would put the PR's config back over the base-branch copy."

The `"pr-"` prefix is written twice: in `mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "pr-"))` and in `basename(scratch).slice("pr-".length)`. If one changes without the other, the tag and branch names go wrong silently. Use one constant, or use `basename(scratch)` whole as the tag.

`plantCommit` reads the six identity fields by position from `--format=%an%n%ae%n%aI%n%cn%n%ce%n%cI` and maps them to env keys by order. Reordering either side silently swaps author and committer. A small helper that builds the identity env would own that coupling.

`clean` holds every clean-case outcome, flagged ones included, so the name reads as "the unflagged ones" in `${flagged}/${clean.length} clean cases flagged`. Calling it `cleanCases` would read correctly.
